note: Monday A, first weekday of workplace English（职场英语）: 事 si6 ×3, then BBC 6 Minute English “Rude emails” (~6 min). No morning Cantonese. After the listen: 60-sec intro to your new team (point → reason → example), say it aloud before 📜. Hard interview lines in tiny recall sets — cue + keywords only, say the line BEFORE flipping, then one from-memory run of each set. Recap Saturday workplace lines, 4 new cards (3 BBC + 1 first-week request). 加油！

tasks.prompt: Warm-up: say 事 (si6, low flat tone 低平调) three times in a row. Low and flat, not mid like 試 si3.
tasks.script: 事 si6 · 事 si6 · 事 si6 (low, flat, no rise)

tasks.prompt: 60 seconds, workplace English: introduce yourself to your new team. Point → reason → example. Say it aloud before opening the script.
tasks.script:
Hi, I'm Junnai. I've just joined the team, and I'll be supporting overseas visa work.
Point: My main goal this week is to learn the process end to end.
Reason: I need to see where applications usually get stuck, so I can help properly.
Example: I'll shadow one case from document check to submission and write down the steps. If anything is unclear, I'll ask early.

questions.explain: 事 si6 is low and flat. 低平调。

questions.q: BBC 6 Minute English: who sent the email asking US government workers to list five things they had accomplished that week, or resign?
questions.explain: The answer in the episode is c) Elon Musk (Phil had guessed JD Vance).

questions.q: get something off your plate means…
options: pass a task or problem to someone else
put a meeting in your calendar
questions.explain: 把任务从自己的待办里推给别人。

questions.q: Best order for your 60-sec team intro?
questions.explain: 先说重点，再讲原因，最后举例。

questions.q: “Would you have ten minutes later to walk me through how this usually works?” is for…
options: politely asking a colleague to show you a process
telling your manager the work is late
questions.explain: 第一周礼貌请教：先问有没有时间，再请对方带你走一遍流程。
